title: Wood-Fired Neapolitan Pizza Dough
steps: Mix roughly 80% of the flour with all the water, yeast and salt until combined and resembling a stiff batter. If using a stand mixer, mix slowly for 2 minutes.
Let the mixture rest for 20 minutes.
Mix at medium speed or knead by hand for 6–8 minutes, adding the remaining flour gradually. The dough should just form a ball and remain very sticky.
Turn out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead briefly, then fold the dough in thirds, seal the seam, rotate and bring the ends together, sealing again. Place seam-side down.
Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and let rise for 90 minutes to 2 hours, until nearly doubled.
Turn out gently and divide into the desired portions; the source suggests about four 200 g balls. Shape gently into balls with taut surfaces and sealed seams.

Cover the dough balls and let rest about 1 hour before shaping. If using later, refrigerate the covered balls. The source also offers an overnight refrigerator proof as an alternative to the bulk rise.
reviewFlags: The source provides weight and volume formulations that may not be equivalent; choose one formulation and review the salt quantity. The stated total dough weight is approximate.
headnote: A direct dough from Forno Bravo’s Wood-Fired Pizza guide. The source recommends weighing ingredients and provides an alternative volume formulation.
sourceNote: Adapted from Forno Bravo, Wood-Fired Pizza (2007), https://www.fornobravo.com/
